directive: Combat-first balance: the fighting is the hook, tactical mechanics create depth, and progression exists to send players back into deity battles.
designPillars: The battle is the primary screen, memory, and hook; management supports fighting but never replaces it.
Every deity must feel individually powerful through animation, impact, enemy reaction, scale, and distinct ability identity.
Challenge comes from readable decisions, positioning, timing, objectives, enemy behavior, and battlefield interaction before stat inflation.
Momentum/Divinity and faction mechanics must create in-battle spend/save decisions across campaign, raid, repeatable, and future modes.
Progression should make the player want to immediately return to battle to see what changed.
Mobile sessions must resolve meaningful combat turns quickly while keeping tactical depth in setup windows and objective pressure.

Defender.fun: turn enemy intent into visible protection decisions
Defender.scalesBy: more simultaneous objective threats, not raw HP walls
Defender.campaign: hold lanes, escort, survive ritual turns
Defender.raid: main objective anchor during boss phase tells

Battery.fun: bank tempo and choose when to spike economy
Battery.scalesBy: tighter resource windows and harder drain enemies
Battery.raid: phase transfer battery and burst-cycle planner

Controller.fun: make terrain and pathing feel like a weapon
Controller.challenge: mobile enemies, cleanse lanes, blocked line of sight
Controller.scalesBy: lane complexity and enemy movement rules
Controller.raid: phase arena rewrites and add control

Breaker.fun: crack defenses through setup then release
Breaker.raid: boss shield phases and break-check moments

Disruptor.fun: bait, fake, and steal enemy tempo
Disruptor.scalesBy: smarter intent variance, not random chaos
Disruptor.campaign: caster denial, wave tempo, trap rooms

Sustain.fun: outlast danger through mastery, not passive healing

Artillery.challenge: cover, forced movement, engagement, sight denial

Guardian.fun: choose what matters most and intercept it
Guardian.scalesBy: more declared threats and priority ambiguity
Guardian.campaign: protect civilians/relics, relic procession, ritual defense
Guardian.raid: protect raid objects during boss tells

Assassin.fun: set the omen, risk the dive, cash execution
Assassin.campaign: priority kills, mage hunts, boss adds
Assassin.raid: delete phase adds and exploit boss vulnerability

campaignMission.purpose: teach and test one mechanic at a time, then combine mechanics by chapter
campaignMission.balanceRule: Normal missions target one primary deity role and one soft alternative; hard missions add one counter-tag and one objective tension.

chapterBoss.purpose: force mastery of a faction mechanic without requiring a specific deity
chapterBoss.balanceRule: Boss phases must include one role-favored answer, one neutral answer, and one dangerous greedy answer.

raid.purpose: scale mastery for weekly/repeatable play while preserving solo active-Titan clarity
raid.balanceRule: Raid difficulty uses phase modifiers, add density, and recovery windows before increasing boss HP/damage.

weeklyTrial.purpose: rotate constraints to make unused Titans valuable
weeklyTrial.balanceRule: Reward problem solving; never make a trial require an owned Legendary.

ascension.balanceRule: Every 5 floors introduces a new verb; every 10 floors increases numerical pressure.

asyncArena.balanceRule: Snapshot AI must preserve counterplay tells and cap sustain loops.

futureModes.purpose: reuse the same contracts for co-op, events, or challenge dungeons
futureModes.balanceRule: New modes cannot introduce bespoke hidden currencies that bypass Momentum/Divinity/faction meters.

combatFeelLevers: hit stop and screen shake budget

antiPatterns: passive sustain loops that ignore objectives
hidden counters with no visual tell
resource denial stacked with no comeback window
raid mechanics that bypass solo active-Titan clarity
Menu-heavy core loop where players manage stats longer than they fight.
deity kits differentiated only by health and damage numbers.
Beautiful battlefield spaces with no tactical purpose.
Difficulty driven mainly by enormous enemy health pools.
Progression systems that feel like spreadsheets before play.
Basic combat actions hidden behind multiple menus.

rebalanceTriggers: role win rate below 42% or above 68% in Normal band
raid phase fail rate above 70% after tell exposure
single deity pick rate above 22% for a mode

acceptanceGates: All 9 roles have mode contracts and counterplay.
All 7 faction mechanic families map to Momentum/Divinity and terrain.
Campaign, raid, weekly, ascension, arena, and future modes have scaling contracts.
No tuning rule requires a specific deity or paid rarity.
Balance audit can run from repository data without external services.

combatFirstDoctrine.corePrinciple: The fighting is the hook. Tactical mechanics create depth. Progression creates long-term retention.
combatFirstDoctrine.primaryExperience: The primary screen and primary player memory must be the deity battle, not menu management.
combatFirstDoctrine.systemServiceTest: Every system must make the deity battle more fun, more tactical, more satisfying, or more replayable. If it does not, reconsider whether it belongs in the core experience.

combatFirstAcceptanceGates.rule: Playable Ops and future game views must present battle selection/simulation before management statistics.
Titan differentiation must include attack identity, ability behavior, range/mobility/role expression, or battlefield interaction.
Battlefield data and mission profiles must expose tactical purpose, objective pressure, or terrain function.
Progression framing must explicitly return the player to battle instead of menu management.
Difficulty guidance must prefer AI, positioning, objective, layout, timing, boss, and composition levers before stats.
Combat design must target cinematic memorable events during battles.

playerExperienceQuestions: Is the player spending most of their time doing something fun?
Would the player willingly play another battle immediately?
